description: List first and last give its ends, as Kotlin and Rust spell them
A sensor's newest reading follows a later push through last
The head of a queue follows a shift through first
Kotlin's first with a predicate finds the first cheap price
last with a predicate searches from the back, as findLast does
A predicate that accepts nothing gives null, as find does
A standing first over an empty list takes the first item pushed
A class's first and last instances are its first and latest created
code:
class Order(item):
    this.item = item
Order("tea")
Order("cake")
[Order.first().item, Order.last().item]

description: A standing last over a class follows each new instance
code:
class Visit(name):
    this.name = name
latest = Visit.last()
Visit("ana")
Visit("bo")
latest.name

description: A class without instances has null as its first and last
A class-level rule keeps each sensor's newest reading
code:
class Sensor(name):
    this.name = name
    this.readings = []
$Sensor.newest = $Sensor.readings.last()
fan = Sensor("fan")
fan.readings.push(3, 9)
fan.newest

description: The first pending task follows the property its predicate reads and new tasks
code:
class Task(title, done):
    this.title = title
    this.done = done
Task("a", true)
b = Task("b", false)
pending = Task.first(task -> !task.done)
b.done = true
Task("c", false)
pending.title

description: A count is not a predicate, so first raises find's error with its own name
code:
xs = [1, 2]
try:
    r = xs.first(2)
catch error:
    r = error
r

description: A program that caught the former error now receives the last item
code:
xs = [5]
try:
    r = xs.last()
catch e:
    r = "caught"
r

description: A failed replacement rolls back through a standing last
code:
stock = ["bolt"]
newest = stock.last()
failure = ""
try:
    stock = 7
catch error:
    failure = error
[failure, newest]
